title: The Nisan-Szegedy bound on relevant variables is never tight, and R_3 = 10: paper, proofs, audited search and Lean certificate
description: Paper (PDF and LaTeX source), hand proofs, an independent exhaustive search with every raw log, the reports of independent referee rounds, a one-command verification script, and a Lean 4 / Mathlib project (zero sorry, standard axioms only, no native_decide) certifying 23 structural theorems, for the results: for every d >= 3 the Nisan-Szegedy bound R_d <= d 2^(d-1) on the number of relevant variables of a degree-d Boolean function is never attained, and the exact value R_3 = 10 (attained by the Chiarelli-Hatami-Saks style function Xi_3). The exhaustive search confirming the finite statement F(11) has no solution is audited computation; F(11) and F(12) are not yet machine-checked. Produced with Claude (Anthropic) language-model agents under the author's direction; the superseded first search and every referee-caught error are preserved rather than removed.
notes: Mathematics Subject Classification 2020: 06E30 (primary), 68Q06, 05D05. Paper, proofs and reports are CC BY 4.0; code, logs and solution files are MIT (see LICENSE).
